semantically_equivalent_models.justification: While GPT-NeoX and GPT-J are not the same, they belong to the same family of models developed by EleutherAI, aiming to replicate the capabilities of OpenAI's GPT models.
GPT-J-6B is a version of GPT-J and is semantically close to GPT-NeoX, both being from EleutherAI and serving as alternatives to models like GPT-3.

parent_models.justification: GPT is the general model architecture upon which different variants like GPT-NeoX, GPT-2, GPT-3, etc. are built.
GPT-XL represents a larger version of GPT models, presumably capturing larger-sized variants like NeoX.
As a predecessor to GPT-NeoX's design intent, GPT-3 represents a lineage of the style of language models.

closest_parent_model.justification: GPT-XL is a more direct reference to large-scale GPT models, aligning with the architecture style and scale goals of GPT-NeoX.

child_models.justification: As a derivative of the GPT-J framework, GPT-J-6B can be considered a specialization or variant model that is more specific about the architecture.

closest_child_model.justification: Amongst the models derivative and more specific than GPT-NeoX, GPT-J-6B directly falls under the same intent of being a large-scale EleutherAI model.

sibling_models.justification: Within the same ecosystem of models produced by EleutherAI, GPT-J acts as a sibling to NeoX as it shares similar goals and design.
Both GPT-3 and GPT-NeoX are positioned as high-performance language models.

closest_sibling_model.justification: GPT-J is closest due to sharing the developers and similar architectural inspirations and purpose with GPT-NeoX.

unrelated_models.justification: GPT-2 is significantly older and less capable, with a different architectural and performance target compared to NeoX.
GPT-3.5, though part of the GPT-3 series, is from a different development cycle and team.
GPT-4 represents a newer generation that likely involves different technological strategies and improvements.
GPT-2-xlarge refers to a variant of GPT-2 and is relatively outdated in comparison.
GPT-4 series variants signify updates and enhancements beyond the scope of NeoX’s design goals.
Another variant from the GPT-4 line, reinforcing the inherent separation in design and target application compared to NeoX.
Incremental improvements and features of GPT-4 that differ from NeoX’s lineage.
A specialized and enhanced GPT-4 that doesn't align directly with the architectural lineage of NeoX.
Though closer to the GPT-3 line, it gains sophistication that aligns it more closely with newer models.
GP seems to poorly specify any relevant architecture in the defined context of GPT models.
Appears as an unrelated or less-connected acronym or model not fitting neatly into the GPT line.
PCT is distinctly not in the same family or nature as GPT models, likely belonging to another model class entirely.
As a graph attention model, GAT is unrelated in design focus and application area to GPT or derivatives.
Stands outside the GPT architecture nomenclature suggesting it targets different applications or functions.
